nodes.summary: For $d \ge 1$ and a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, this is the kd-tree built from the list by alternating-axis median splits, starting with split axis $0$.
nodes.title: Kd-tree construction from the first axis

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$, let $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$ be an axis and let $P$ be a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. The kd-tree built from $P$ starting at axis $a$ is the empty tree if $P$ is empty and the leaf holding $p$ if $P = [p]$. If $P$ has $n \ge 2$ points, sort $P$ by $a$-coordinate with merge sort, let $L$ be the first $\lfloor n/2 \rfloor$ points of the sorted list and $R$ the remaining ones. The result is the…
nodes.title: Kd-tree construction by median splits

nodes.summary: For an axis $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$ and a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$, this is the $a$-coordinate of the first point of the list, or $0$ if the list is empty.
nodes.title: First-point coordinate

nodes.summary: For $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the point $p$ lies in the closed axis-aligned box $[lo, hi]$ when $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$.
nodes.title: Membership in an axis-aligned box

nodes.summary: A kd-tree over points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ is either empty, a leaf holding one point of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, or a split node holding a split axis $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, a split value $s \in \mathbb{Z}$ and two kd-trees, its left and right subtrees.
nodes.title: Kd-trees

nodes.summary: For every kd-tree $t$, the list of the points stored in $t$, read from left to right, has length equal to the size of $t$, the number of points stored in $t$.
nodes.title: Length of the point list of a kd-tree

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$, let $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$, let $P$ be a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. Then $p$ occurs in the range report, for the box $[lo, hi]$, of the kd-tree built from $P$ by median splits starting at axis $a$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $P$ and $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Membership in the range report of a built kd-tree

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$, let $P$ be a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and let $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. Then $p$ occurs in the range report, for the box $[lo, hi]$, of the kd-tree built from $P$ by median splits starting at axis $0$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $P$ and $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Range report of a kd-tree built from the first axis

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a kd-tree over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ that satisfies the kd invariant, and let $lo, hi, p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$. Then $p$ occurs in the range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ if and only if $p$ is one of the points stored in $t$ and $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Range report of a valid kd-tree

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$, let $a \in \{0, \dots, d-1\}$ and let $P$ be a list of points in $\mathbb{Z}^d$. A point $p \in \mathbb{Z}^d$ is stored in the kd-tree built from $P$ by median splits starting at axis $a$ if and only if $p$ occurs in $P$.
nodes.title: A built kd-tree holds the same points as its input

nodes.summary: For a dimension $d \ge 1$ and an axis $a \in \{0, \dots, d - 1\}$, the next split axis is $(a + 1) \bmod d$, so the axes are visited cyclically.
nodes.title: Next split axis of a kd-tree

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a valid kd-tree over $\mathbb{Z}^d$, let $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, and let $acc$ be a list of points. The accumulator range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ onto $acc$ equals the list of points of $t$, in left-to-right order, that lie in the box (the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$), followed by $acc$.
nodes.title: Accumulator range report of a valid kd-tree

nodes.summary: Points are vectors in $\mathbb{Z}^d$ with coordinates $p_0, \dots, p_{d-1}$; the box $[lo, hi]$ consists of the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every $i$. For a kd-tree $t$ and a list $acc$ of points, the accumulator report of $t$ for $[lo, hi]$ onto $acc$ is defined by recursion on $t$. For the empty tree it is $acc$. For a leaf $p$ it is $p$ followed by $acc$ if $p$ lies in the box, and $acc$…
nodes.title: Accumulator range report of a kd-tree

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$. For every starting axis $a$, every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and all $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the range report for the box $[lo, hi]$ of the kd-tree built from $P$ starting at axis $a$ is a permutation of the list of entries of $P$ that lie in the box, that is, the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Range report of a built kd-tree up to order

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$. For every starting axis $a$, every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and all $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, let $T$ be the kd-tree built from $P$ starting at axis $a$. The range report of $T$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ equals the list of points of $T$, in left-to-right order, that lie in the box, that is, the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Range report of a built kd-tree as a filter

nodes.summary: For every valid kd-tree $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and all $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ equals the list of points of $t$, in left-to-right order, that lie in the box, that is, the points $p$ with $lo_i \le p_i \le hi_i$ for every coordinate $i$.
nodes.title: Correctness of the kd-tree range report

nodes.summary: For a kd-tree $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and $lo, hi \in \mathbb{Z}^d$, the range report of $t$ for the box $[lo, hi]$ is the accumulator range report of $t$ for $[lo, hi]$ onto the empty list.
nodes.title: Orthogonal range report of a kd-tree

nodes.summary: Let $d \ge 1$. For every starting axis $a$ and every list $P$ of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the size of the kd-tree built from $P$ starting at axis $a$ equals the length of $P$ (repeated points counted with multiplicity).
nodes.title: Size of a built kd-tree

nodes.summary: The size of a kd-tree is defined by recursion: the empty tree has size $0$, a leaf has size $1$, and a split node has the sum of the sizes of its two children. Since points are stored only at leaves, this is the number of points stored in the tree, counted with multiplicity.
nodes.title: Size of a kd-tree

nodes.summary: For every kd-tree $t$ over $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and every list $acc$ of points, the accumulator traversal of $t$ onto $acc$ equals the list of points of $t$ in left-to-right order followed by $acc$.
nodes.title: Accumulator traversal of a kd-tree

nodes.summary: For a kd-tree $t$ over points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$ and a list $\mathit{acc}$ of such points, the accumulator traversal of $t$ onto $\mathit{acc}$ is $\mathit{acc}$ when $t$ is empty, the point $p$ followed by $\mathit{acc}$ when $t$ is a leaf holding $p$, and, when $t$ is a split node with left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, the traversal of $L$ onto the traversal of $R$ onto $\mathit{acc}$.
nodes.title: Kd-tree point traversal with an accumulator

nodes.summary: For $d \ge 1$, every axis $a$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the point list of the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $a$ is a permutation of the list.
nodes.title: Building a kd-tree preserves its points

nodes.summary: For $d \ge 1$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the point list of the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $0$ is a permutation of the list.
nodes.title: Building a kd-tree from axis 0 preserves its points

nodes.summary: For a split node with axis $a$, split value $s$, left subtree $L$ and right subtree $R$, the point list of the node is the point list of $L$ followed by the point list of $R$.
nodes.title: Point list of a kd-tree split node

nodes.summary: The point list of a kd-tree is the list of the points stored at its leaves, from left to right.
nodes.title: Point list of a kd-tree

nodes.summary: For $d \ge 1$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $0$ satisfies the kd invariant.
nodes.title: Kd-trees built from axis 0 satisfy the kd invariant

nodes.summary: For $d \ge 1$, every axis $a$ and every list of points of $\mathbb{Z}^d$, the kd-tree built from the list by median splits starting at axis $a$ satisfies the kd invariant.
nodes.title: Median-split kd-trees satisfy the kd invariant

nodes.summary: A kd-tree satisfies the kd invariant when at every split node, with axis $a$ and split value $s$, every point of the left subtree has $a$-coordinate at most $s$ and every point of the right subtree has $a$-coordinate at least $s$.
nodes.title: Kd invariant

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
